newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lower orange juice sales, price hit Dreyfus Citrus.
newsitem.headline: Lower orange juice sales, price hit Dreyfus Citrus.

text.p: Louis Dreyfus Citrus, the world's third largest producer of orange juice, said on Thursday lower sales volume in the United States and weaker prices hit business in the first half of fiscal year 1996/97.
In a statement the company said sales fell 10.7 percent to $194.1 million in the July to December 1996 period from $218.1 million in the same period a year ago.
But better operating margins helped offset the sales decline, resulting in improved earnings for the first half of fiscal year 1996/97, it said.
The company however did not provide earnings data for the first half.
Louis Dreyfus Citrus said it had expected sales to decline after selling last year in the United States an unsually high volume of orange juice produced by other processors.
It also said low margin sales were partly offset by higher sales of orange juice produced by the company in Brazil and imported into the United States.
It expects to partly make up for sales volume through its new plant in Winter Garden, Florida, which was aquired in September 1996 and started processing in November 1996.
Orange juice prices fell by almost 30 percent between September 1996 and December 1996 to $1,050 per metric tonne in Europe, in response to large crops in Brazil and Florida.
But the company managed to limit the impact of lower prices through participation contracts, fixed price sales commitments and orange juice contracts on the New York Cotton Exchange.

It also said the outlook for the rest of fiscal year 1996/97 is positive as it will benefit from strong orange juice demand, notably in Europe, and from the combined results of its hedging programme, participation contracts and fixed price sales.
Louis Dreyfus Citrus was listed on the Paris bourse second marche in November 1996.
